name: r2_ttw_plain_voice
rationale: Merges think_then_write's silent board-verification step with plain_voice's register bans (no markdown/hype/generic filler) to try to get plain_voice's human-score gain without losing D0's faithfulness.
instruction:
Before writing, work through the position silently: identify the piece that moved, its origin and destination square, and what it now attacks, defends, or opens up -- check each claim against the actual diagram, not memory or assumption. Check whether the opponent has an immediate reply that answers the point you're about to make. Do not show this reasoning; no headers, no steps.

Then write 1-4 plain sentences in the voice of a human annotator typing notes on their own game -- first or third person, ordinary prose, no markdown, no bold, no bullets, no move restated in brackets or with an exclamation point. Do not use hype or engine-voice adjectives ("thematic", "ambitious", "solidify", "signals intent", "razor-sharp", "dynamic", "crashing through"). Do not pad with generic phrases that would fit any position ("complex middlegame", "maintains the tension", "plenty of resources"). Say only what is specific to this move and true on the board. If your silent check finds nothing concrete and verified beyond the obvious, write one short, modest sentence rather than inventing a threat. Output only the commentary.

name: r2_ttw_plain_voice_hedged
rationale: Same merge as (a) but additionally caps the model to at most one verified concrete threat and pushes it toward plans/evaluations instead of tactical claims, since concrete claims are where both prior winners went wrong.
instruction:
Before writing, work through the position silently: identify the piece that moved, its origin and destination square, and what it now attacks, defends, or opens up -- check each claim against the actual diagram, not memory. Do not show this reasoning or use headers.

Write 1-4 plain sentences in the voice of a human annotator noting their own game -- ordinary prose, no markdown, no bold, no bullets, no hype adjectives ("thematic", "ambitious", "solidify", "razor-sharp", "dynamic"), no generic filler that would fit any position. Prefer plans, ideas, and evaluations of the position over concrete tactical claims: what the move develops, what square or file it gives up or gains, what plan it continues. Name at most one concrete threat -- a specific piece taking a specific square next move -- and only if you have verified it is actually available on this board; otherwise mention no concrete threat at all. Never say who stands better unless the material count makes it obvious. If nothing concrete and verified stands out, write one short, modest sentence. Output only the commentary.

name: r2_ttw_plain_voice_short
rationale: Under-90-word compression of (a) to test whether the verification+register instructions survive terseness without losing effect.
instruction: Silently verify against the board: what piece moved, from where to where, and what it now attacks, defends, or opens -- check the diagram, not memory. Don't show this work. Then write 1-4 plain sentences in a human annotator's own-game voice: ordinary prose, no markdown, bold, bullets, or bracketed move restatements. Skip hype/engine adjectives ("thematic", "ambitious", "solidify", "dynamic") and generic filler ("complex middlegame", "maintains tension"). State only what's specific and verified. If nothing verified stands out, write one modest sentence instead of inventing a threat. Output only the commentary.

name: r2_single_piece_scope
rationale: Novel idea from reading failures: most faithfulness errors (wrong-piece, hallucinated-threat, wrong-eval, wrong-move) came from claims about a piece other than the one that moved or about who stands better, so this restricts every claim to the moved piece and its one direct interaction and bans evaluation and alternative-move claims entirely.
instruction:
Before writing, silently locate the moved piece's start and end square on the diagram and its immediate reach from there -- what it now directly attacks, defends, captures, or blocks. Verify against the actual diagram, not memory. Do not show this work or use headers.

Then write 1-4 plain sentences, ordinary prose, no markdown, bold, bullets, or hype adjectives ("thematic", "ambitious", "solidify", "dynamic"), in a human annotator's own-game voice. Restrict every claim to the moved piece and the one piece it directly interacts with -- what it captures, checks, or is captured by -- do not describe what any other piece on the board threatens, plans, or is doing, and do not say who stands better or worse unless this move changes the material count. Do not mention an alternative move, a different line, or what "could have been played instead." If the moved piece's own action is all there is to say, say only that in one short sentence rather than reaching for a second, unverified claim. Output only the commentary.
